name: book-to-wiki-graph
description: Convert books into scope-aware introductions, fully attributed TOC indexes, LLM-led teaching atoms, audited relation graphs, and three-level knowledge constellations.

interface.shortDescription: Turn books into atomic Wiki graphs.
interface.longDescription: Convert a book PDF to Markdown, derive fully attributed and independently readable open-depth organizer indexes, jointly review category-specific atom boundaries and local teaching logic, distinguish instructional prompts from knowledge bridges and reflection questions, run a three-pass global relation audit before materialization, then write fully attributed primary atoms, definition-only named concept cards, formula cards, and deterministic Canvas maps together.
defaultPrompt: Convert this PDF into a TOC-centered Wiki graph.
Give every organizer note queryable source, parent, level, hierarchy, count, date, and review properties.
Audit and repair this book graph with category-aware atomization and relation feedback.

Let the LLM exclusively determine knowledge boundaries and count: distinguish complete knowledge, parallel formal definitions, solved examples, exercises, introductions, and post-knowledge reflection questions before materialization.

Keep section-wide framing questions first, attach inline practice to its knowledge topic, preserve independently reusable concepts, and split adjacent parallel definitions even without transition words.
Use the knowledge-relation mapper to build a three-pass atom-concept teaching graph.
Build three-level knowledge constellations with hidden derived cards, collapsed exercise entries, reviewed major-method examples, and labelled organization edges.
Render a sibling PNG for every Canvas and require a PNG-backed logic-first review before completion.
Preserve and explicitly classify every printed 观察、思考、尝试、交流、探究 marker; never silently discard activity context.
Treat a preface, chapter introduction, section introduction, and single-topic motivation as distinct scenario scopes; never split one scoped introduction into paragraph or image fragments.
Reject organizer ownership that crosses the next printed heading or leaves an instructional subsection with exercises only.
